WHAT THIS TESTS

Relevant wind, limited task coverage

The short central passage: the intended wind opposes B → A, so learning it should change the value of taking that route. The western bypass is a shorter alternative than the long route around the central cluster.

The eastern yard: accessible aisles with a proposed secondary airflow, but no monitoring target. Baseline 4 includes the whole yard in its global uncertainty criterion. The proposed method uses the unchanged clarity-valued path mask.

The key difference from Scenario 3: the proposed airflow puts wind on a useful monitoring passage. Its effect must be demonstrated in the next simulation.

WHAT IS ALREADY VERIFIED

Geometry, not a claimed winner

    All methods retain the same unknown-wind prior, physical dynamics, POAM, MBD budget and RPCBF. The background monitoring target is explicitly zero for every method; clarity still evolves everywhere. No wind-support mask is given to the robot.

    Remote observations can still influence the task through GP correlations. A zero acquisition weight does not force zero covariance.

    NEXT EXPERIMENT / DECLARED BEFORE RESULTS

    Check the airflow, then compare equal elapsed time

    1. One bounded CFD pilot. Use physical roof inlets and floor outlets with the existing 3-D solver. Check the stationary wind at the robot plane: strong opposing flow in the short gap, a traversable weaker-wind bypass, and low wind inside A/B. Reject the airflow design if this does not happen.
    2. Check route execution. Run the same double integrator, wind-force mapping and RPCBF on the generated alternatives. Confirm the wind actually changes transit performance; do not infer this from arrows.
    3. Paired learning comparison. Baseline 4 learns globally until its uncertainty threshold, then runs 300 s of MBD. The proposed method uses the same total elapsed time. Begin with one pair; expand to the three declared B starts only after the pilot passes.
    4. Report all outcomes. Compare learning duration and mean clarity deficit over the shared time, plus final deficit, contacts and planning time. Keep failed trials. Full MBD runtime and any advantage over global learning remain unmeasured for this layout.
    Proposed physical airflow boundary conditions

    This is a covered 8 × 6 × 2 m workspace with 1.5 m columns. Angled roof inflow and nearby floor pressure outlets are proposed to localize a jet across the short gap and a milder flow in the eastern yard. All other boundaries are no-slip. Peak inlet speeds are not robot-plane speeds. The existing stationary-mean CFD model will determine the interior velocities; no interior wind is painted or rescaled.
